title: Long-Term Changes in Wintering Waterbirds of a Predominantly Managed and Human-Modified Lagoon Complex: The Caorle Lagoon (NE Italy), 1993–2022
content: We analysed International Waterbird Census data from the Caorle Lagoon (northern Adriatic, Italy), collected during 1993–2022, to assess changes in abundance, diversity, community composition, habitat distribution and thermal affinity in a wetland complex dominated by fish farms managed for waterbird hunting. Across 29 censuses, 947,541 in-dividuals belonging to 84 species were recorded, excluding raptors. Total abundance in-creased significantly and more than doubled, while species richness and Shannon diver-sity also increased. Ducks, geese and swans, particularly grazing feeders, showed the strongest positive trends, whereas coots and rails declined. Low similarity between the first and last censuses indicated substantial community reorganisation, including in-creasing goose and Eurasian Teal Anas crecca abundance and reduced Eurasian Coot Fulica atra dominance. Fish farms supported 80.9% of all individuals, while the contribution of large, reclaimed areas increased from 0.7% in 1994–2002 to 10.2% in 2012–2022. Abun-dance-weighted Community Temperature Index showed no significant temporal trend or relationship with local winter temperature. However, presence-weighted CTI increased, whereas CTI excluding the five most abundant species declined. These contrasting results highlight the influence of community weighting on thermal indicators. Overall, the Caorle lagoon supported increasing wintering numbers alongside pronounced compositional and spatial changes, consistent with an important role of managed wetlands and sur-rounding agricultural habitats.
